sanskrit: bibhidus te maṇistambhān karṇāṭṭaśikharāṇi ca bhagnonmathitavegāni yantrāṇi ca vicikṣipuḥ
english: They shattered the jewelled pillars and the turret-tops of the ramparts, and hurled away the war-engines, their mechanisms broken and crushed by the force.

sanskrit: parigṛhya śataghnīś ca sacakrāḥ sahuḍopalāḥ cikṣipur bhujavegena laṅkāmadhye mahābalāḥ
english: The mighty ones seized the śataghnis — fitted with wheels and loaded with spiked stones — and flung them by the strength of their arms into the midst of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: prākārasthāś ca ye ke cin niśācaragaṇās tadā pradudruvus te śataśaḥ kapibhiḥ samabhidrutāḥ
english: Whatever bands of night-roamers stood upon the battlements then fled in hundreds, driven away by the onslaught of the monkeys.

sanskrit: tatas tu rājavacanād rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ niryayur vikṛtākārāḥ sahasraśatasaṃghaśaḥ
english: Then, at the king's command, the shape-shifting rākṣasas poured out in hundreds of thousands, wearing hideous forms.

sanskrit: śastravarṣāṇi varṣanto drāvayanto vanaukasaḥ prākāraṃ śodhayantas te paraṃ vikramam āsthitāḥ
english: Raining down showers of weapons and routing the forest-dwellers, they cleared the ramparts and stood forth in supreme valor.

sanskrit: sa māṣarāśisadṛśair babhūva kṣaṇadācaraiḥ kṛto nirvānaro bhūyaḥ prākāro bhīmadarśanaiḥ
english: By those night-wanderers resembling heaps of black gram — terrible to behold — the battlements were once again cleared of monkeys.

sanskrit: petuḥ śūlavibhinnāṅgā bahavo vānararṣabhāḥ stambhatoraṇabhagnāś ca petus tatra niśācarāḥ
english: Many foremost monkeys fell with their bodies pierced by spears; and there too the night-roamers fell with pillars and gate-arches shattered upon them.

sanskrit: keśākeśy abhavad yuddhaṃ rakṣasāṃ vānaraiḥ saha nakhair dantaiś ca vīrāṇāṃ khādatāṃ vai parasparam
english: A hair-grappling battle raged between the rākṣasas and the monkeys, the warriors tearing at each other with claws and teeth.

sanskrit: niṣṭananto hy ubhayatas tatra vānararākṣasāḥ hatā nipatitā bhūmau na muñcanti parasparam
english: Groaning on both sides, those monkeys and rākṣasas, slain and fallen to the ground, did not release their grip on one another even then.

sanskrit: rāmas tu śarajālāni vavarṣa jalado yathā tāni laṅkāṃ samāsādya jaghnus tān rajanīcarān
english: Rāma for his part rained volleys of arrows like a thunder-cloud; reaching Laṅkā, those arrows slew the night-wanderers.

sanskrit: saumitrir api nārācair dṛḍhadhanvā jitaklamaḥ ādiśyādiśya durgasthān pātayām āsa rākṣasān
english: And Saumitri too, with iron arrows, his bow firm and his weariness conquered, selecting his marks one after another, felled the rākṣasas stationed in the fortress.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyavahāro 'bhūt sainyānāṃ rāghavājñayā kṛte vimarde laṅkāyāṃ labdhalakṣo jayottaraḥ
english: Then, by Rāghava's command, the armies withdrew, having wrought destruction in Laṅkā, the objective gained and victory assured.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato niviśamānāṃs tān sainikān rāvaṇānugāḥ abhijagmur gaṇān eke piśācakṣudrarakṣasām
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, as those soldiers were retiring to camp, some of Rāvaṇa's followers — troops of piśācas and lesser rākṣasas — fell upon them.

sanskrit: parvaṇaḥ pūtano jambhaḥ kharaḥ krodhavaśo hariḥ prarujaś cārujaś caiva praghasaś caivam ādayaḥ
english: Among them were Parvana, Pūtanā, Jambha, Khara, Krodhavaśa, Hari, Prarujas, Āruja, Praghasas, and others of that ilk.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipatatāṃ teṣām adṛśyānāṃ durātmanām antardhānavadhaṃ tajjñaś cakāra sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Then, as those evil-souled ones swooped down while remaining invisible, Vibhīṣaṇa, who knew the secret of slaying those concealed, worked their destruction.

sanskrit: te dṛśyamānā haribhir balibhir dūrapātibhiḥ nihatāḥ sarvaśo rājan mahīṃ jagmur gatāsavaḥ
english: Made visible, O king, they were slain on all sides by the powerful monkeys who struck from afar, and fell lifeless to the earth.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ sabalo rāvaṇo niryayāv atha vyūhya cauśanasaṃ vyūhaṃ harīn sarvān ahārayat
english: Then Rāvaṇa, unable to endure this, sallied forth with his full force, arraying the formation known as the Cauśanasa, and drove against all the monkeys.

sanskrit: rāghavas tv abhiniryāya vyūḍhānīkaṃ daśānanam bārhaspatyaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā pratyavyūhan niśācaram
english: But Rāghava, marching out to meet the ten-faced one who had drawn up his army, adopted the Bārhaspatya disposition and counter-arrayed against the demon.

sanskrit: sametya yuyudhe tatra tato rāmeṇa rāvaṇaḥ yuyudhe lakṣmaṇaś caiva tathaivendrajitā saha
english: Coming together there, Rāvaṇa fought with Rāma; and Lakṣmaṇa likewise fought with Indrajit.

sanskrit: virūpākṣeṇa sugrīvas tāreṇa ca nikharvaṭaḥ tuṇḍena ca nalas tatra paṭuśaḥ panasena ca
english: Sugrīva fought with Virūpākṣa; Nikharvaṭa with Tāra; and Nala there with Tuṇḍa, and Paṭuśa with Panasa.

sanskrit: viṣahyaṃ yaṃ hi yo mene sa sa tena sameyivān yuyudhe yuddhavelāyāṃ svabāhubalam āśritaḥ
english: Whoever deemed another his match engaged him: each at the hour of battle took his stand relying on the strength of his own arms.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāro vavṛdhe bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ lomasaṃharṣaṇo ghoraḥ purā devāsure yathā
english: That encounter grew fierce, multiplying terror in the timid, raising the hair on end, dreadful as the ancient war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo rāmam ānarchac chaktiśūlāsivṛṣṭibhiḥ niśitair āyasais tīkṣṇai rāvaṇaṃ cāpi rāghavaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa assailed Rāma with showers of śaktis, spears, and swords of sharp iron; and Rāghava likewise assailed Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tathaivendrajitaṃ yattaṃ lakṣmaṇo marmabhedibhiḥ indrajic cāpi saumitriṃ bibheda bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: So too did Lakṣmaṇa strike the alert Indrajit with arrows that pierced vital points; and Indrajit in turn struck Saumitri with many shafts.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaḥ prahastaṃ ca prahastaś ca vibhīṣaṇam khagapatraiḥ śarais tīkṣṇair abhyavarṣad gatavyathaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa fought with Prahasta, and Prahasta with Vibhīṣaṇa, each drenching the other with sharp arrows feathered with bird-plumes, unwavering in the fight.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ balavatām āsīn mahāstrāṇāṃ samāgamaḥ vivyathuḥ sakalā yena trayo lokāś carācarāḥ
english: The clash of those mighty wielders of great weapons was such that all three worlds, with all their moving and unmoving creatures, trembled.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ prahastaḥ sahasā samabhyetya vibhīṣaṇam gadayā tāḍayām āsa vinadya raṇakarkaśaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then Prahasta, rough in battle, suddenly charged at Vibhīṣaṇa and struck him with his mace, roaring aloud.

sanskrit: sa tayābhihato dhīmān gadayā bhīmavegayā nākampata mahābāhur himavān iva susthiraḥ
english: Though struck by that mace of terrible force, the wise and mighty-armed Vibhīṣaṇa did not waver — firm as the Himālaya itself.

sanskrit: tataḥ pragṛhya vipulāṃ śataghaṇṭāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ abhimantrya mahāśaktiṃ cikṣepāsya śiraḥ prati
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, seizing his great missile adorned with a hundred bells, charged it with a mighty spell and hurled it straight at Prahasta's head.

sanskrit: patantyā sa tayā vegād rākṣaso 'śaninādayā hṛtottamāṅgo dadṛśe vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ
english: Struck by it as it fell with the roar of a thunderbolt, the rākṣasa was seen with his head torn away, like a tree shattered by the wind.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ saṃkhye prahastaṃ kṣaṇadācaram abhidudrāva dhūmrākṣo vegena mahatā kapīn
english: Seeing Prahasta, that night-roamer, slain in battle, Dhūmrākṣa charged with great speed against the monkeys.

sanskrit: tasya meghopamaṃ sainyam āpatad bhīmadarśanam dṛṣṭvaiva sahasā dīrṇā raṇe vānarapuṃgavāḥ
english: Seeing his army rushing forward, fearful to behold like a storm-cloud, the foremost monkeys were suddenly panic-stricken in the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tān sahasā dīrṇān dṛṣṭvā vānarapuṃgavān niryāya kapiśārdūlo hanūmān paryavasthitaḥ
english: Then, seeing those foremost monkeys suddenly seized with fear, Hanūmān — tiger among monkeys — issued forth and stood firm before them.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvāvasthitaṃ saṃkhye harayaḥ pavanātmajam vegena mahatā rājan saṃnyavartanta sarvaśaḥ
english: Seeing the son of the Wind standing steady in the fight, O king, the monkeys rallied with great swiftness on every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīt tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ rāmarāvaṇasainyānām anyonyam abhidhāvatām
english: Then a great tumultuous clamor arose, thrilling the hair on end, as the armies of Rāma and Rāvaṇa charged against each other.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte saṃgrāme ghore rudhirakardame dhūmrākṣaḥ kapisainyaṃ tad drāvayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: As that dreadful battle raged, turning the ground to a mire of blood, Dhūmrākṣa routed the monkey host with his arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ rākṣasamahāmātram āpatantaṃ sapatnajit tarasā pratijagrāha hanūmān pavanātmajaḥ
english: Hanūmān, son of the Wind, that slayer of enemies, swiftly intercepted that great minister among rākṣasas as he charged forward.

sanskrit: tayor yuddham abhūd ghoraṃ harirākṣasavīrayoḥ jigīṣator yudhānyonyam indraprahlādayor iva
english: A dreadful battle ensued between those two heroes — monkey and rākṣasa — each striving to conquer the other in combat, like Indra and Prahlāda of old.

sanskrit: gadābhiḥ parighaiś caiva rākṣaso jaghnivān kapim kapiś ca jaghnivān rakṣaḥ saskandhaviṭapair drumaiḥ
english: The rākṣasa struck the monkey with maces and iron clubs; and the monkey struck the demon with trees — branches and boughs and all.

sanskrit: tatas tam atikāyena sāśvaṃ sarathasārathim dhūmrākṣam avadhīd dhīmān hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Then the wise Hanūmān, son of the Wind, slew the massive-bodied Dhūmrākṣa along with his horses, chariot, and charioteer.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā dhūmrākṣaṃ rākṣasottamam harayo jātavisrambhā jaghnur abhyetya sainikān
english: Then, seeing that foremost rākṣasa Dhūmrākṣa slain, the monkeys, their confidence restored, closed in and struck down the enemy soldiers.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā balibhir haribhir jitakāśibhiḥ rākṣasā bhagnasaṃkalpā laṅkām abhyapatan bhayāt
english: Slaughtered by those powerful, victorious monkeys, the rākṣasas, their resolve broken, fled in terror toward Laṅkā.

sanskrit: te 'bhipatya puraṃ bhagnā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ sarvaṃ rājñe yathāvṛttaṃ rāvaṇāya nyavedayan
english: Those night-wanderers, routed and reduced to the remnant that survived, rushed into the city and reported all that had happened to King Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rāvaṇas tebhyaḥ prahastaṃ nihataṃ yudhi dhūmrākṣaṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ sasainyaṃ vānararṣabhaiḥ
english: Hearing from them that Prahasta had been slain in battle, and Dhūmrākṣa the great bowman along with his army, by those foremost of monkeys —

sanskrit: sudīrgham iva niḥśvasya samutpatya varāsanāt uvāca kumbhakarṇasya karmakālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: — Rāvaṇa breathed a long sigh, sprang from his excellent throne, and said: "The time for Kumbhakarṇa's work has come."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā vividhair vāditraiḥ sumahāsvanaiḥ śayānam atinidrāluṃ kumbhakarṇam abodhayat
english: Having said so, he had Kumbhakarṇa — who lay plunged in deepest slumber — roused by various instruments of enormously loud sound.

sanskrit: prabodhya mahatā cainaṃ yatnenāgatasādhvasaḥ svastham āsīnam avyagraṃ vinidraṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ tato 'bravīd daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: Having with great effort awakened him — with no trace of distress upon himself — the lord of rākṣasas waited until he sat composed and alert and free of sleep; then Daśagrīva spoke to the mighty Kumbhakarṇa:

sanskrit: dhanyo 'si yasya te nidrā kumbhakarṇeyam īdṛśī ya imaṃ dāruṇaṃ kālaṃ na jānīṣe mahābhayam
english: "You are fortunate, Kumbhakarṇa, that your sleep is such — for you know nothing of this dreadful time of great peril.

sanskrit: eṣa tīrtvārṇavaṃ rāmaḥ setunā haribhiḥ saha avamanyeha naḥ sarvān karoti kadanaṃ mahat
english: This Rāma, crossing the ocean with a bridge and with his monkeys, holds us all in contempt and is working great carnage here.

sanskrit: mayā hy apahṛtā bhāryā sītā nāmāsya jānakī tāṃ mokṣayiṣur āyāto baddhvā setuṃ mahārṇave
english: I carried off his wife, Sītā by name, the daughter of Janaka; and to rescue her he has come, having built a bridge across the great ocean.

sanskrit: tena caiva prahastādir mahān naḥ svajano hataḥ tasya nānyo nihantāsti tvad ṛte śatrukarśana
english: By him, Prahasta and many other great kinsmen of ours have been slain. There is no one but you to kill him, O afflicitor of enemies.

sanskrit: sa daṃśito 'bhiniryāya tvam adya balināṃ vara rāmādīn samare sarvāñ jahi śatrūn ariṃdama
english: So gird yourself and march out today, O best of the mighty, and slay all the enemies — Rāma and the rest — in battle, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: dūṣaṇāvarajau caiva vajravegapramāthinau tau tvāṃ balena mahatā sahitāv anuyāsyataḥ
english: The two younger brothers of Dūṣaṇa — Vajravega and Pramāthin — will follow you with great strength at your side."

sanskrit: ity uktvā rākṣasapatiḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ tarasvinam saṃdideśetikartavye vajravegapramāthinau
english: Having spoken thus, the lord of rākṣasas instructed the swift Kumbhakarṇa in what must be done, and likewise Vajravega and Pramāthin.

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu tau vīrau rāvaṇaṃ dūṣaṇānujau kumbhakarṇaṃ puraskṛtya tūrṇaṃ niryayatuḥ purāt
english: Saying "So be it" to Rāvaṇa, those two warriors — the younger brothers of Dūṣaṇa — placing Kumbhakarṇa at their head, quickly marched out of the city.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato viniryāya purāt kumbhakarṇaḥ sahānugaḥ apaśyat kapisainyaṃ taj jitakāśy agrataḥ sthitam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then Kumbhakarṇa, having issued forth from the city with his followers, beheld that monkey army standing before him with the bearing of victors.

sanskrit: tam abhyetyāśu harayaḥ parivārya samantataḥ abhyaghnaṃś ca mahākāyair bahubhir jagatīruhaiḥ karajair atudaṃś cānye vihāya bhayam uttamam
english: The monkeys quickly rushed up to him, surrounding him on all sides; some struck him with many great tree-trunks, others raked him with their claws — casting aside all fear.

sanskrit: bahudhā yudhyamānās te yuddhamārgaiḥ plavaṃgamāḥ nānāpraharaṇair bhīmaṃ rākṣasendram atāḍayan
english: Those monkeys, fighting in many ways by many modes of warfare, struck the dreadful lord of rākṣasas with every manner of weapon.

sanskrit: sa tāḍyamānaḥ prahasan bhakṣayām āsa vānarān panasaṃ ca gavākṣaṃ ca vajrabāhuṃ ca vānaram
english: As he was being struck he laughed and began to devour the monkeys — Panasa, Gavākṣa, and the monkey Vajrabāhu among them.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā vyathanaṃ karma kumbhakarṇasya rakṣasaḥ udakrośan paritrastās tāraprabhṛtayas tadā
english: Seeing the devastating deeds of Kumbhakarṇa the demon, Tāra and the other monkey chiefs cried out in terror.

sanskrit: taṃ tāram uccaiḥ krośantam anyāṃś ca hariyūthapān abhidudrāva sugrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇam apetabhīḥ
english: Seeing Tāra crying out and the other monkey chieftains in distress, Sugrīva charged at Kumbhakarṇa without fear.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipatya vegena kumbhakarṇaṃ mahāmanāḥ śālena jaghnivān mūrdhni balena kapikuñjaraḥ
english: Then that great-souled foremost of monkeys charged swiftly and struck Kumbhakarṇa on the head with a śāla tree, with great force.

sanskrit: sa mahātmā mahāvegaḥ kumbhakarṇasya mūrdhani bibheda śālaṃ sugrīvo na caivāvyathayat kapiḥ
english: Though the great-souled, swift Sugrīva split the śāla tree upon Kumbhakarṇa's head, the monkey did not succeed in paining him.

sanskrit: tato vinadya prahasañ śālasparśavibodhitaḥ dorbhyām ādāya sugrīvaṃ kumbhakarṇo 'harad balāt
english: Then Kumbhakarṇa, roused by the touch of the śāla tree, roared with laughter, seized Sugrīva in both arms, and carried him off by force.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇaṃ tu sugrīvaṃ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasā avekṣyābhyadravad vīraḥ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ
english: Seeing Sugrīva being carried off by the demon Kumbhakarṇa, the heroic Saumitri — the joy of his friends — rushed forward.

sanskrit: so 'bhipatya mahāvegaṃ rukmapuṅkhaṃ mahāśaram prāhiṇot kumbhakarṇāya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: Charging in, Lakṣmaṇa — slayer of enemy heroes — dispatched a great arrow with golden fletching at Kumbhakarṇa with tremendous force.

sanskrit: sa tasya dehāvaraṇaṃ bhittvā dehaṃ ca sāyakaḥ jagāma dārayan bhūmiṃ rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ
english: That shaft, piercing through his armor and his body, passed on and split the earth, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: tathā sa bhinnahṛdayaḥ samutsṛjya kapīśvaram kumbhakarṇo maheṣvāsaḥ pragṛhītaśilāyudhaḥ abhidudrāva saumitrim udyamya mahatīṃ śilām
english: His heart thus pierced, Kumbhakarṇa the great bowman released the king of monkeys, and — taking up a massive boulder for a weapon — charged at Saumitri, raising the great rock aloft.

sanskrit: tasyābhidravatas tūrṇaṃ kṣurābhyām ucchritau karau ciccheda niśitāgrābhyāṃ sa babhūva caturbhujaḥ
english: As he charged swiftly, Lakṣmaṇa severed his two upraised arms with two razor-headed shafts of keen edge; he became four-armed.

sanskrit: tān apy asya bhujān sarvān pragṛhītaśilāyudhān kṣuraiś ciccheda laghv astraṃ saumitriḥ pratidarśayan
english: All those arms of his too, still grasping their boulder-weapons, Saumitri severed with razor-arrows, displaying swiftness of hand in archery.

sanskrit: sa babhūvātikāyaś ca bahupādaśirobhujaḥ taṃ brahmāstreṇa saumitrir dadāhādricayopamam
english: Though he grew even more immense and many-footed and many-headed and many-armed, Saumitri burned him — mountain-piled as he was — with the Brahmāstra.

sanskrit: sa papāta mahāvīryo divyāstrābhihato raṇe mahāśanivinirdagdhaḥ pādapo 'ṅkuravān iva
english: That mighty warrior, struck by the divine weapon, fell in battle — scorched as if by a mighty thunderbolt, like a flowering tree blasted down.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛtrasaṃkāśaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ tarasvinam gatāsuṃ patitaṃ bhūmau rākṣasāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: Seeing the swift Kumbhakarṇa — terrible as Vṛtra — lifeless and fallen to the ground, the rākṣasas fled in fear.

sanskrit: tathā tān dravato yodhān dṛṣṭvā tau dūṣaṇānujau avasthāpyātha saumitriṃ saṃkruddhāv abhyadhāvatām
english: Seeing those warriors fleeing thus, the two younger brothers of Dūṣaṇa rallied the troops and then, blazing with fury, charged at Saumitri.

sanskrit: tāv ādravantau saṃkruddhau vajravegapramāthinau pratijagrāha saumitrir vinadyobhau patatribhiḥ
english: Saumitri received those two — Vajravega and Pramāthin — as they charged in fury, meeting them both with arrows, roaring aloud.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ yuddham abhaval lomaharṣaṇam dūṣaṇānujayoḥ pārtha lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: Then a very tumultuous battle ensued, thrilling the hair on end, O Pārtha, between the two brothers of Dūṣaṇa and the wise Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: mahatā śaravarṣeṇa rākṣasau so 'bhyavarṣata tau cāpi vīrau saṃkruddhāv ubhau tau samavarṣatām
english: He drenched those two rākṣasas with a great rain of arrows; and those two fierce warriors, furious, drenched him in return — both of them together.

sanskrit: muhūrtam evam abhavad vajravegapramāthinoḥ saumitreś ca mahābāhoḥ saṃprahāraḥ sudāruṇaḥ
english: For a moment the dreadful combat between Vajravega and Pramāthin on one side and the mighty-armed Saumitri on the other continued thus.

sanskrit: athādriśṛṅgam ādāya hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ abhidrutyādade prāṇān vajravegasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the Wind, seizing a mountain peak, charged and took the life of the demon Vajravega.

sanskrit: nīlaś ca mahatā grāvṇā dūṣaṇāvarajaṃ hariḥ pramāthinam abhidrutya pramamātha mahābalaḥ
english: And Nīla the monkey, of great strength, charging with a huge rock, crushed Pramāthin — the younger brother of Dūṣaṇa.
